chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to buy the green crop?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy crops before they are harvested in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility (jawaaz) of purchasing crops while they are still green (akhdar) and standing in the field, a practice often debated in contrast to the prohibition of *gharar* (uncertainty). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that there is no religious impediment, reflecting the Shia juristic view that such transactions are valid provided the essential elements of the crop are identifiable, thereby facilitating agricultural trade and land ownership. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic commercial law in accommodating practical economic needs while maintaining contractual clarity.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is it Permissible to buy the green plants?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Bukayr ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following:
“Upon my asking abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about buying a plantation when it only is green, he (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
